drafted_from: tool:read-rows-from-a-rest-service row in tool-rows.json, do-work/read-rows.mjs, read-data/hosts.json and test/read-rows.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Read the first 5 active rows of the members table in my Supabase project https://example-project.supabase.co, columns id and name, ordered by id." It runs tool:read-rows-from-a-rest-service with your connection and shows the rows and the total.
no_lists_because: It names no list: it reads one table of your connected database service and answers rows, a count and a total, writing nothing.
instructions: 1. Connect your PostgREST service (a Supabase project is one) so a service connection such as service_connection:supabase holds its service key; the key is never part of the request.

2. Say which table and which rows; your AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:read-rows-from-a-rest-service and input {account_id, project_url, table, select, filters, order, limit, offset}.

3. Read the answer {rows, count, total}: count is the rows in this page (limit at most 1000), total the whole table's matching rows when the service reports it; ask again with offset to read the next page.

4. Filters are column to "operator.value" with eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, like, ilike, is or in; a refused key (401 or 403) means connect the service again; the key goes only to a project under supabase.co.

worked_examples.title: Five active members, two columns, ordered by id
worked_examples.ask: Read the first 5 active rows of members in my project, columns id and name.
worked_examples.given: From tools/read-rows-from-a-rest-service/test/read-rows.test.mjs (the service replaced by a stand-in): the tool sends one GET to https://example-project.supabase.co/rest/v1/members?select=id,name&limit=5&order=id.asc&status=eq.active with the key as apikey and Bearer headers; the service answers one row {id: 1, name: "Example Member"} with content-range 0-0/11.
worked_examples.hands_back: {rows: [{id: 1, name: "Example Member"}], count: 1, total: 11}. A 401 answers "The service refused the held key (401). Connect the service again with a current key."; a project_url under another domain is refused before any request with "the key is not sent anywhere else".
